verdict.rationale: Aider is itself an official command-line tool. It has documented installation, files named on the command line, many command-line switches mirrored in config files and AIDER_xxx environment variables, and a non-interactive `--message` mode that runs one instruction and exits for scripting. Community users corroborate both interactive and scriptable CLI use. The unsupported-scripting note covers only the Python API, not the CLI. Missing for 10: no evidence of structured or machine-readable CLI output (e.g. JSON) for agent consumption.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Aider has many options which can be set with command line switches.
aider --message "make a script that prints hello" hello.js
I only use Aider interactively, but I really should consider Aider in the 'scriptable' sense more
